title: On-Demand ISR: revalidateTag & Cache Tags Indexing

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Imagine a warehouse full of labeled boxes. Multiple documents are marked with a blue sticker called 'products'. When a product price changes, the manager announces 'throw out all blue-stickered boxes'. The warehouse instantly purges only those items without having to discard or re-check the rest of the warehouse.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `revalidateTag` allows you to purge specific entries from the Next.js Data Cache on demand. When fetching data, attach a tag: `fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['products'] } })`. When a mutation occurs (like in a Server Action), call `revalidateTag('products')`. The next time someone requests that data, Next.js refreshes it from the upstream source instead of serving stale cached data.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, Cache Tagging creates an inverted index mapping custom tag strings to cache entries in the Next.js Data Cache. Calling `revalidateTag(tag)` invalidates all corresponding cache entries across various routes and pages atomically. In Next.js 15, `revalidateTag` purges the Data Cache and marks the associated server-side Route Cache segments as stale, triggering re-computation on subsequent requests.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: Next.js maintains a tag manifest in its persistent cache handler (file system or distributed store like Redis/S3). When a `fetch` with `next.tags` executes, the response payload hash is associated with the provided tag keys in the manifest. When `revalidateTag(tag)` runs, Next.js increments the revalidation timestamp for that tag. Subsequent cache lookups compare the entry's creation timestamp against the tag's invalidation timestamp; if older, it treats the entry as a cache miss.

rosettaStone.react: Custom cache invalidation using TanStack Query `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey })`.
rosettaStone.angular: Service-worker cache tagging or manual HTTP interceptor cache clearing.

codeComparison.title: Time-based polling vs On-Demand Tag Revalidation
codeComparison.summary: Time-based polling serves stale data or wastes compute; on-demand tag revalidation invalidates data immediately upon mutation.

legacyOrBad.label: Time-based Revalidation
legacyOrBad.snippet: fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 3600 } }); // ❌ OLD: Stale for up to 1 hour

modernOrGood.label: Tag-based Invalidation
modernOrGood.snippet: revalidateTag('products'); // ✅ NEW: Instant on-demand cache purge

interviewGotchas.question: What is the difference between `revalidatePath` and `revalidateTag`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers want to see if you understand the scope of cache invalidation.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: `revalidatePath` purges both the Full Route Cache and Data Cache for a specific URL path structure (including or excluding sub-routes). `revalidateTag` purges the underlying Data Cache entries across any page or component in the application that fetched data using that tag, without being bound to a single URL path.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: `revalidatePath` can cause over-invalidation of unrelated data on a page, whereas `revalidateTag` surgically invalidates only the shared entity.

interviewGotchas.question: Does `revalidateTag` purge data synchronously in the current request or on the next request?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: This tests knowledge of server action lifecycle and read-your-own-writes semantics.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: In Next.js, calling `revalidateTag` inside a Server Action marks the tag invalid. During the same server action response pass, Next.js re-renders the current route tree with the freshly fetched data so the client sees the updated state in one round-trip.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Calling `revalidateTag` in an external webhook handler invalidates the cache for *future* incoming requests, not for clients currently viewing the page without navigation.
